generator.params.blade_tilt.why: Bracken holds its broad triangular blade out nearly level on top of its upright stipe.

rules.generator.params.blade_tilt.note: Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001), fig. 13.104.1 (Pteridium aquilinum var. pubescens): a broad triangular frond seen from above, held horizontal; fig. 13.104.3 A: a long upright stipe under a triangular tripinnate blade. The 45 degrees at the blade's foot, with the bend every frond takes along its length, is the model's reading of nearly level.

traits.note: Abrams's flora (vol. 1, 1923; ferns by Maxon): a slender, branching rhizome creeping far underground, fronds borne singly along it; blades pinnately decompound; sori in a continuous line along the margin, covered by the blade's own rolled-back edge (with a minute inner indusium).
